$comment: PK 1.7.0: the Angkor Cel-Diorama look (docs/VISUAL_BIBLE.md). The land, buildings and water are stylised PBR (real light, material weight); people and animals are flat NPR toon (a stepped light ramp, an ink outline, a rim). Everything here is a tuning knob, the three.js twin of Godot's inspector. Colours are sRGB hex. on = the preset uses it (config/quality.json kingdom.diorama).

camera.$comment: HD-2D: a long lens (low field of view) from further away flattens the view like a model village. fov in degrees; the framing stays as it was at the old 32 degrees.

post.$comment: Tilt-shift: the band of sharp focus across the middle (share of the screen height) and how strong the blur grows toward the top and bottom (px). Grade: warm golden highlights against cool blue shadows; contrast around mid grey; saturation.

units.$comment: NPR toon for people, animals and the court. ramp = the light steps from dark to lit (0-1 light falling on the surface) and the brightness of each band; shadowTint colours the dark band (cool, Genshin-like); outlinePx = ink line width in screen pixels; rim = edge light strength.

terrain.$comment: Splat by slope and height: laterite red on inclines and banks, bright emerald on flat lowland, dry paddy earth in patches. slope: 0 = flat, 1 = a wall; the red comes in between slopeFrom and slopeTo. aoSteps: the block shadows in hollows and at the foot of slopes come in this many hard steps, aoStrength how dark the deepest step is.

water.$comment: Prek canal water: no mirrors. Depth fade from shallow jade over the silt bed to deep teal (m); the sky is faked by Fresnel (power) with a stepped sky colour by time of day; the sun glints in a sharp 2-step cel highlight; a crisp foam line where water meets the bank (m of depth); two slow ripple layers drift against each other (speed m/s, scale m).

elephantGrass.$comment: PK 1.8.0: elephant grass (ស្មៅដំរី) and cogon grass (ស្បូវ), dense tropical grass that rolls in the wind: the three.js port of PK's Godot spatial shader (all motion is vertex displacement; one noise fetch per vertex). It grows in broad wild stands on open land (standTiles = stand size in tiles, cover = share of open land inside stands, perTile = clumps per tile inside a stand) and in a fringe on the land along rivers and canals (bank = chance per shore tile; never on the water); never on worn earth, roads, fields, unexplored land or within keepAway tiles of a building. count = most clumps at once (near the view; reach = share of the view distance planted). height = elephant grass height range (m); spread = a tussock's width (m, wider than tall: dense stands); PK: from the landscape view the grass stays under 1 m, with natural variation (taller inside a stand, shorter at its edge, each clump its own). cogon = dense cogon grass (ស្បូវ, Imperata cylindrica, the thatch grass of Cambodian roofs): share of clumps, its height range (m) and a paler tint; it flowers in white plumes. dry = the colour dry clumps wash toward, dryShare = share of dry clumps, flowering = share of clumps with white plumes. Wind: strength (x the weather's wind), dirDeg (0 = east, 90 = south on the map), speed = how fast the gust waves travel (m/s), waveScale = 1 / gust wave size (m), sharpness (0 soft .. 0.45 crisp bands), baseBend = lean in calm air, gustBend = extra lean in a gust, sway / swaySpeed = slow rocking, flutter / flutterSpeed = leaf-tip flutter. gustSheen = leaves turn pale in a gust (shows the wave), baseDark = darkness inside the clump. trample = how near (m) a walker bends it away. lod = shrink from/to (share of the planted radius). The tall grasses of the Tonle Sap plains (Saccharum, Phragmites; called elephant grass) flower in white plumes; Pennisetum purpureum, the 'elephant grass' of Africa, came later. confidence: GAMEPLAY_ABSTRACTION.

atmosphere.$comment: PK 1.8.0 (references: a humid jungle clearing, high humidity atmospheric fog, volumetric light rays breaking through the clouds). mist: soft banks of ground mist drifting low (height in m) round the view, one per world cell of `cell` m at most (count), size in m; thickness = weather share (weather), + dawn x the dawn (Anachak Khmer's day) + wet x how wet the ground is after rain; opacity at full thickness; color by day, nightColor by night. shafts: beams of sunlight slanting from the sun through gaps in the clouds (count, one per cell), width and length in m, strength; brightness = weather share + afterRain x wetness on a clear or cloudy day; none at night. Colours sRGB.

seeThrough.$comment: PK 1.8.0: zoomed in close, buildings, trees and tall grass between the camera and the people at work turn see-through round them, so the acting people and animals can always be seen. Fully on when the camera stands nearer than zoom[0] m, off beyond zoom[1] m (the RTS zoom runs 28 to 150 m). targets = how many people and animals (nearest the middle of the view, the selected first) get a window; radius = the window's width in m (it is 1.6 times as tall); amount = how much of the cover is taken away in its middle (a screen-door dither, so it stays sharp and cheap).

detail.$comment: Ground detail near the camera: undergrowth in the forest, a few wild flowers, pebbles, reeds and lotus pads at the water. The open meadow is drawn by the ground itself (no scattered tufts: PK 1.7.0). Counts are the most drawn at once. PK 1.8.0 (the jungle clearing reference): mossy laterite rocks (forest floor, its edge, banks, a few on open land and earth), fallen palm fronds and creeping roots (forest floor and its edge).

ground.$comment: PK 1.7.0 (reference: a Manor Lords-like settlement): the ground follows life. Bare earth where people live and work (round buildings, yardTiles wide) and where they walk (each step wears the grass: walkWear per second on the tile, workWear while working); it grows back slowly (regrow per 10 s) where nobody goes. soilFrom/soilTo: how worn (0-1) before the earth shows through and is all earth. Meadow: a fine natural lawn of several greens; forest floor darker. Colours sRGB. PK 1.8.0: the earth is red laterite mud (Angkor's red soil), dark where it is wet.

wet.$comment: PK 1.8.0 (reference: a red clay jungle path with puddles reflecting the cloudy sky): in rain or storm the ground soaks (soak per second, 0..1) and dries after (dry per second: about 6 minutes). Wet ground darkens (darken), the mud paths most; puddles stand in the hollows of the mud (puddleScale = 1 / hollow size in m, puddleCover = share of the mud), mirror the sky colour (sky, sRGB) and shine; falling drops ring them.

light.$comment: Sun and shadow for the diorama: a lower afternoon sun (elevation in degrees) gives long, readable shadows; shadowMap px; fill = the sky's soft fill light (lower = deeper shadows); sun = sunlight strength. foliage multiplies the trees' colours (deeper, natural greens), each tree a little different.
